findings.scenario: While steering during planning, a lane hazard appears and viewers propose clear_lane.
findings.gap: No status contract covers hazard timing, route progress, action eligibility, or cost.
findings.recommendation: Show route and hazard timers plus one action preview; provide a counter/abstain control that requires no chat reading.

findings.scenario: Viewers favor clearing the lane while the streamer steers toward the deadline.
findings.gap: Streamer veto, confirmation, override, and movement interruption are undefined.
findings.recommendation: Set streamer authority, confirmation rules, movement interaction, and a safe no-response default before resolution.

findings.scenario: The streamer monitors proposals and a deadline through repeated 20/5/5 cycles.
findings.gap: Information priority and consequences are unspecified, risking chat-driven cognitive overload.
findings.recommendation: Prioritize one legal action and plain-language consequence, collapse raw chat, and keep abstention available.

findings.scenario: A viewer on a phone submits clear_lane as the 20-second planning window closes over a slow or unstable connection.
findings.gap: The plan says late input is rejected and duplicates are idempotent, but defines no authoritative receipt time, acknowledgment, retry behavior, or visible rejection reason.
findings.recommendation: Define server-receipt phase cutoffs and idempotency keys; return a mobile-readable pending/accepted/rejected status with a reason, and never make retries create extra influence.

findings.scenario: An anonymous viewer refreshes or switches devices and submits again during the same turn.
findings.gap: “Eligible viewer” and one-influence-per-viewer lack an identity/session boundary, while identity and privacy expectations are unspecified.
findings.recommendation: Define a privacy-preserving per-turn pseudonymous identity and reset rule, what anonymous participation permits, and how duplicate sessions are handled without exposing account identity.

findings.scenario: A large audience exceeds configurable K, or a small cohort needs bot backfill, while viewers use chat or a touch control.
findings.gap: Cohort selection, tie handling, fairness across turns, and accessible mobile action feedback remain open; visibility of bots alone does not explain whose input counted.
findings.recommendation: Publish a deterministic, auditable N-to-K selection and rotation rule, distinguish human and bot influence, and provide touch-sized controls plus a clear counted/not-counted receipt.

findings.scenario: Continuous movement reaches the blocked lane and clear_lane loses or is unavailable.
findings.gap: Collision response and hazard duration are open, allowing an indefinite stop or undefined penalty.
findings.recommendation: Define collision effects, hazard expiry, and bounded recovery. Keep physics deterministic and local; the character is not a model driving physics.

findings.scenario: A near-deadline collision causes a wipe with route stages remaining.
findings.gap: Wipe, checkpoint, recovery, and continuation rules provide no defined return path.
findings.recommendation: Define wipe triggers, respawn, recovery costs, and who ends the match; preserve no-permanent-control-loss and no-unavoidable-death limits.

findings.scenario: A proposal arrives at cutoff as movement collides with the hazard.
findings.gap: Clock authority, event order, and boundary state are unspecified.
findings.recommendation: Define a monotonic clock, receipt cutoff, and deterministic boundary snapshot for both modes; model output cannot advance the character.

findings.scenario: A participant creates or controls many anonymous/pseudonymous accounts and submits once through each, multiplying influence despite the per-viewer limit.
findings.gap: Eligible-viewer identity, admission, and account-to-influence binding are unspecified; N-to-K does not itself constrain Sybils.
findings.recommendation: Bind one influence unit to a privacy-preserving authenticated platform subject per turn; set admission and aggregate caps, and keep bot identities separate.

findings.scenario: A coordinated group shards submissions across cohorts or manipulates the eligible denominator while K or tie rules are configurable, steering normalization without exceeding any one cohort's apparent cap.
findings.gap: Cohort assignment, roster timing, normalization denominator, quorum, and tie handling are unresolved.
findings.recommendation: Freeze eligible roster and cohort assignments before each turn; specify denominator, minimum participation, per-cohort caps, and deterministic tie handling.

findings.scenario: A bot-heavy group repeatedly backfills participation or induces wipe/survival outcomes that create or enlarge a simulated bounty, then routes value to an attacker-controlled eligible viewer.
findings.gap: Bot rewards are prohibited, but bounty provenance, creation authority, trigger accounting, and bot influence on bounty adjustments remain open.
findings.recommendation: Require explicit human authorization and traceable source for each bounty; exclude bots from funding, eligibility, and payout, and cap adjustments across retries and wipes.

findings.scenario: The attacker reapplies the bounded hazard on successive turns, consuming every counter window and leaving no practical recovery before the deadline.
findings.gap: No permanent control loss or unavoidable death is stated, but frequency, cumulative pressure, cooldown, and guaranteed recovery are not defined.
findings.recommendation: Set per-phase and match-wide pressure caps, cooldowns, non-stacking effects, and a guaranteed recovery or counter window independent of viewer turnout.

findings.scenario: A late chat message contains instructions aimed at the language model to propose an out-of-phase or stronger action; it is mistaken for control text rather than untrusted viewer content.
findings.gap: Natural language is only a proposal and local validation is required, but the prompt/data boundary and strict action mapping are not specified.
findings.recommendation: Treat chat as untrusted data, never as instructions; map it only to an enumerated action schema and enforce phase, eligibility, and effect bounds locally after model output.

findings.scenario: A reconnect or offline replay resubmits a previously accepted event under a new request and applies its influence twice, possibly in a later turn.
findings.gap: Duplicate and late input should be rejected/idempotent, but durable deduplication scope and session/turn binding are unspecified.
findings.recommendation: Use stable event IDs with durable deduplication bound to session and turn; reject stale sequence numbers and ensure replay cannot mint a new eligible event.

findings.scenario: The provider or network fails during a presentation, then recovers with queued submissions.
findings.gap: Offline fixture is promised, but failover, stale-input, and recovery rules are absent.
findings.recommendation: Define health signals and offline controls; discard or revalidate queued actions and document safe recovery/rollback.

findings.scenario: The stage presents a plan rehearsal, fixture, replay, or match as evidence.
findings.gap: No provenance labels distinguish critique, fixture events, simulated bounty, and observed outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Label source and mode on views/exports, mark bounty simulated with no payout, and preserve event IDs and phase times.

findings.scenario: Audience reads fictional Twitch or IVS concepts as integrations or sponsorship.
findings.gap: Stage copy, brand assets, and data disclosures are unspecified.
findings.recommendation: Label concepts simulated, use only approved assets, and disclose no affiliation or live platform data.

findings.scenario: A route or service delay threatens the event deadline during the 20/5/5 loop.
findings.gap: There is no show runbook, hard-stop policy, or mode-switch authority.
findings.recommendation: Set the demo budget, cue/hold/restart controls, and labeled offline fallback so the show ends on time without implying success.

findings.scenario: A viewer submits through chat and buttons, reconnects, then replays a prior-turn command.
findings.gap: Eligibility identity, cross-channel deduplication and idempotency retention are undefined.
findings.recommendation: Bind server-issued identity, match, turn and action ID; atomically consume one influence unit across channels and reject stale epochs. Specify reconnect and retention rules.

findings.scenario: Chat instructs the model to grant authority; its otherwise valid proposal arrives after resolution starts.
findings.gap: Schema validation alone does not bind proposal authority, deadline or original intent.
findings.recommendation: Treat chat as untrusted data; allowlist commands and arguments, bind proposals to immutable viewer/turn provenance, enforce server arrival deadlines and discard late completions without transferring influence.

findings.scenario: An operator receives a modified or replayed data-only hotfix manifest.
findings.gap: Trusted approver, artifact authenticity and anti-rollback contracts are unspecified.
findings.recommendation: Require explicit approval, pinned artifact hash and authenticated signer; bind version, base-state/rules hash and expiry. Reject unknown DSL capabilities and activate atomically at a declared boundary.

findings.scenario: Bot backfill is relabeled human during reconnect or recovery and contributes bounty.
findings.gap: Visible bot labels do not establish durable reward provenance.
findings.recommendation: Persist immutable actor origin and eligibility snapshots in an authoritative contribution ledger; exclude synthetic events from bounty creation and reward allocation, including after recovery.

findings.scenario: Offline failover occurs while an action or reward is committed; recovery replays it.
findings.gap: Atomic handover, single-writer authority and reconciliation rules are absent.
findings.recommendation: Specify epoch fencing, checkpoint plus accepted-command ledger, atomic mode switch and exactly-once effect/reward application. Freeze ambiguous commits for reconciliation; label fixture/live provenance separately.

findings.scenario: The moving streamer reaches the obstruction before the viewer counter resolves.
findings.gap: The proposed loop has no defined actionable decision, activation order, collision consequence or movement policy outside planning.
findings.recommendation: Specify a paper timeline connecting readable warning, streamer choice, counter eligibility, activation and recovery. Have the user select controls and consequences; preserve continuous planning movement.

findings.scenario: Unequal squads receive different bot backfill while viewers reconnect or switch submission channels.
findings.gap: One influence per viewer does not establish cohort fairness, stable eligibility, deduplication or defensive balancing.
findings.recommendation: Define identity and per-turn eligibility snapshots across channels; restore bounded cohort weighting and defensive balancing. Present weighting, K, denominator, bot voting and tie policies for human selection.

findings.scenario: Bot-generated danger increases bounty collected by human survivors.
findings.gap: JSON prohibits bots earning rewards but omits the stronger prohibition on bot-created farmable bounty; Markdown only implies human provenance.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly exclude bots and fixture events from human bounty creation and allocation, retaining immutable contribution provenance through recovery. Leave bounty amounts and reward splits for human choice.

findings.scenario: Repeated individually bounded obstructions combine into indefinite control denial or escalating damage.
findings.gap: No permanent control loss and no unavoidable death omit the original explicit bans on stun-lock and unbounded damage, including cumulative effects.
findings.recommendation: Restore both hard prohibitions and specify enforceable aggregate duration, placement, overlap and damage limits with a viable recovery path. Numeric balance values require selection before simulation.

findings.scenario: A timely chat message produces a model proposal after closure while the delivery deadline expires.
findings.gap: Phase durations do not define authoritative receipt versus completion cutoffs, deadline clock, suspension semantics or asynchronous processing.
findings.recommendation: Specify monotonic phase/match clocks, expiry ordering and pause policy. Require asynchronous bounded model work, local revalidation, explicit late rejection and no silent next-turn rollover; never wait for inference in the game loop.

findings.scenario: Provider failure occurs during reward commitment, followed by offline operation and live recovery.
findings.gap: An offline fixture alone does not specify continuity, ownership or duplicate-effect prevention.
findings.recommendation: Define canonical commands, deterministic time/seed, safe-boundary single-writer handover, durable accepted-command/reward records, uninterrupted rendering/simulation and health/state comparison before recovery. Keep fixture provenance visibly separate.

findings.scenario: A staged bullet-time sequence presents a replay as a live model decision.
findings.gap: The baseline omits the original three-minute demo target and actual sanitized message, recorded tool-call, measured latency, validation and execution evidence requirements.
findings.recommendation: Restore the demo evidence contract with persistent live/fixture/replay labels and distinct model, Codex and engine stages. Unmeasured timings or unexecuted integrations must remain explicitly illustrative.

findings.scenario: A character or attacker review agent is interpreted as an autonomous gameplay controller.
findings.gap: Rehearsal perspectives, human actors, avatar state and runtime AI services are conflated.
findings.recommendation: Create an authority table separating streamer navigation, viewer proposals, engine-owned character state, bounded red-team actions, operator controls and advisory AI. Do not infer autonomous character or attacker deployment from role critiques.

findings.scenario: A selected model or passing mock executor is reported as a working gameplay integration.
findings.gap: Routing documentation distinguishes selection from inference, but the product plan lacks an equivalent evidence boundary.
findings.recommendation: Carry task/provider/model/effort, policy and content hashes through a reusable injected-executor boundary. Preserve separate labels for selection, actual critique, mocked transport and observed gameplay; retain disabled providers, explicit budgets and no silent fallback.

findings.scenario: A valid data-only hotfix changes safety limits or replays an obsolete manifest.
findings.gap: Prohibiting executable hot-loading alone does not preserve game authority or establish trusted activation.
findings.recommendation: Specify approver authority, authenticated artifact/base/version binding, bounded DSL capabilities and atomic boundary activation. Revalidate hard safety invariants independently of model output; adopt the security review's anti-replay and recovery contracts.

findings.scenario: Passing PRODUCT's credential-free mock MVP criteria is presented as submission readiness.
findings.gap: Local fixture acceptance does not satisfy the actual Twitch connection and Codex evidence requirements recorded in hackathon research.
findings.recommendation: Separate offline-slice and submission gates. The latter needs evidenced Twitch operation, actual Codex work/session provenance and the required demo; obtain separate implementation/publication authorization. This does not require paid model inference.

limitation: Document review only; no gameplay or runtime behavior verified; stored location terms were mechanically sanitized without fresh agent review

redaction_provenance.operation: mechanical location-term sanitization and hash rebinding
